findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so logs written through it are never recorded
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new instance unrelated to the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a test injects a `*TestLogger` and then checks `InfoLogs.Calls` or `InfoLogs.Ctx` on it, the log entries go to the throwaway instance and the test sees zero calls. That makes `TestLogger` unusable for verifying `LoggerMiddleware`, or anything else that logs through `FromContext`. Returning `f` (or a logger that shares the same `Logs` storage) would keep the recordings.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the changed LoggerMiddleware fields have no tests
findings.body: The plugin/request log fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) used to be added explicitly in `LoggerMiddleware`. They now depend on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` setting contextual attributes, and on that middleware sitting before `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain. No test checks that `instrumentContext` sets these attributes or that the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line still carries them and the traceID. A reordering or a regression in `FromContext` would silently strip these fields from the data-egress logs.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks other implementations
findings.body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is now a required method on the exported `plog.Logger` interface. Any other implementation of `plog.Logger` stops compiling until it adds this method. That includes fakes and wrappers in other packages and in enterprise or external code. The change goes beyond the rename the PR title describes.
